resource.name: aws_ec2_fleet
resource.description: Provides a resource to manage EC2 Fleets.
resource.llm_summary: The `aws_ec2_fleet` Terraform resource enables the creation and management of EC2 Fleets, allowing users to provision and scale diverse EC2 instances across multiple instance types, availability zones, and purchase models (e.g., On-Demand, Spot). It is commonly used for optimizing cost and capacity in dynamic workloads, batch processing, or high-availability applications. Key configurations include instance diversification, allocation strategies, fleet lifecycle management, and automated scaling to meet performance and budget requirements.

examples.title: Basic Usage
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates the basic configuration of the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource to provision EC2 instances using a launch template and spot instances. It showcases the use of the `launch_template_config` block to specify the launch template ID and version, and the `target_capacity_specification` block to define a total target capacity of 5 instances with a default capacity type of "spot."

arguments.name: context
arguments.description: (Optional) Reserved.
arguments.llm_summary: The `context` argument in the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource is a string that allows users to optionally define a reserved identifier or metadata associated with the fleet. While its specific functionality is not detailed, it may be used to tag or reference the fleet in a broader operational or organizational context, aiding in resource tracking or integration with external systems.

arguments.name: excess_capacity_termination_policy
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether running instances should be terminated if the total target capacity of the EC2 Fleet is decreased below the current size of the EC2. Valid values: `no-termination`, `termination`. Defaults to `termination`. Supported only for fleets of type `maintain`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `excess_capacity_termination_policy` argument in the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource allows users to define how the fleet handles running instances when the total target capacity is reduced below the current fleet size. By specifying either `no-termination` or `termination`, users can control whether excess instances are retained or terminated, enabling lifecycle management for fleets of type `maintain` to align with scaling and cost optimization goals.

arguments.name: fleet_state
arguments.llm_summary: The `fleet_state` argument in the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource allows users to specify the desired operational state of the EC2 Fleet, such as `active` or `deleted`. This configuration determines whether the fleet is actively managing instances or has been terminated, enabling users to control the lifecycle and availability of the fleet in alignment with their infrastructure needs.

arguments.name: fulfilled_capacity
arguments.llm_summary: The `fulfilled_capacity` argument in the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource allows users to specify the number of EC2 instances successfully launched and running as part of the fleet. This argument provides insight into the fleet's current capacity fulfillment, enabling users to monitor or define thresholds for scaling and resource allocation based on operational needs.

arguments.name: fulfilled_on_demand_capacity
arguments.llm_summary: "Defines the minimum number of On-Demand instances to be provisioned within the EC2 Fleet, ensuring predictable capacity for workloads requiring guaranteed availability while balancing cost and resource allocation."

arguments.name: id
arguments.llm_summary: The `id` argument in the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource represents the unique identifier of the EC2 Fleet, allowing users to reference or retrieve the fleet's configuration and state after creation. While optional, it is typically used for tracking and managing the fleet programmatically, enabling workflows that require fleet-specific operations or integrations.

arguments.name: replace_unhealthy_instances
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether EC2 Fleet should replace unhealthy instances. Defaults to `false`. Supported only for fleets of type `maintain`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `replace_unhealthy_instances` argument in the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource allows users to control whether the fleet automatically replaces instances identified as unhealthy, ensuring continuous availability and optimal performance. This functionality is only applicable to fleets of type `maintain` and supports user goals related to instance lifecycle management and high availability.

arguments.name: tags
arguments.description: (Optional) Map of Fleet tags. To tag instances at launch, specify the tags in the Launch Template. If configured with a provider `default_tags` configuration block present, tags with matching keys will overwrite those defined at the provider-level.
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags` argument in the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource allows users to define a map of key-value pairs to assign metadata tags to the EC2 Fleet itself, enabling resource organization, identification, and categorization for purposes like cost allocation, environment labeling, or compliance tracking. While it does not directly tag instances launched by the fleet (which must be configured in the Launch Template), it can override provider-level default tags if matching keys are specified.

arguments.name: tags_all
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags_all` argument for the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource allows users to define a comprehensive set of key-value tags that are applied to all resources created within the EC2 Fleet, ensuring consistent metadata and organization across instances. This facilitates resource categorization, cost allocation, and automation workflows by enabling users to uniformly label fleet-managed resources for tracking, filtering, and integration with other AWS services.

arguments.name: terminate_instances
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether to terminate instances for an EC2 Fleet if it is deleted successfully. Defaults to `false`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `terminate_instances` argument in the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource allows users to define the lifecycle behavior of EC2 instances associated with the fleet upon its deletion. When set to `true`, it ensures that all instances launched by the fleet are terminated automatically, supporting cleanup and resource management goals; when left as `false` (default), the instances persist even after the fleet is deleted, enabling continued use or manual management.

arguments.name: terminate_instances_with_expiration
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether running instances should be terminated when the EC2 Fleet expires. Defaults to `false`.
arguments.llm_summary: Controls the lifecycle behavior of the EC2 Fleet by specifying whether running instances should be automatically terminated when the fleet expires. This argument enables users to define instance retention policies, ensuring resources are either preserved for manual management or cleaned up to optimize cost and resource usage.

arguments.name: type
arguments.description: (Optional) The type of request. Indicates whether the EC2 Fleet only requests the target capacity, or also attempts to maintain it. Valid values: `maintain`, `request`, `instant`. Defaults to `maintain`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `type` argument in the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource allows users to define the request behavior for the EC2 Fleet, specifying whether it should only fulfill the target capacity (`request` or `instant`) or actively maintain the capacity over time (`maintain`). This configuration impacts the fleet's lifecycle management, enabling users to align the fleet's provisioning strategy with their workload requirements, such as one-time capacity fulfillment or ongoing resource stability.

arguments.name: valid_from
arguments.description: (Optional) The start date and time of the request, in UTC format (for example, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ). The default is to start fulfilling the request immediately.
arguments.llm_summary: The `valid_from` argument in the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource allows users to define the UTC start date and time for when the EC2 Fleet request begins fulfilling capacity. By specifying this argument, users can control the fleet's activation timing to align with scheduled workloads or deployment windows, ensuring resources are provisioned only when needed.

arguments.name: valid_until
arguments.description: (Optional) The end date and time of the request, in UTC format (for example, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ). At this point, no new EC2 Fleet requests are placed or able to fulfill the request. If no value is specified, the request remains until you cancel it.
arguments.llm_summary: The `valid_until` argument in the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource allows users to define the expiration date and time for the EC2 Fleet request in UTC format, controlling the lifecycle of the fleet's provisioning process. By setting this argument, users can ensure that no new instances are launched after the specified time, aligning resource allocation with time-bound workloads or project deadlines.

blocks.name: fleet_instance_set

arguments.name: instance_ids
arguments.llm_summary: The `instance_ids` argument in the `fleet_instance_set` of the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource allows users to specify a list of EC2 instance IDs to include in the fleet. By defining this argument, users can explicitly control which existing instances are part of the fleet, enabling targeted management and scaling of specific resources within the fleet's configuration.

arguments.name: instance_type
arguments.llm_summary: The `instance_type` argument in the `fleet_instance_set` of the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource allows users to specify the EC2 instance type (e.g., `t2.micro`, `m5.large`) for the fleet's instances. By defining this argument, users control the compute capacity, performance characteristics, and cost profile of the instances within the fleet, enabling tailored resource allocation to meet workload requirements.

arguments.name: lifecycle
arguments.llm_summary: The `lifecycle` argument in the `fleet_instance_set` of the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource allows users to specify the operational lifecycle of instances within the fleet, such as whether they are `spot` or `on-demand`. Configuring this argument helps define the cost model and availability strategy for the instances, enabling users to optimize resource allocation based on budget and workload requirements.

arguments.name: platform
arguments.llm_summary: The `platform` argument in the `fleet_instance_set` of the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource allows users to specify the operating system or virtualization platform for the instances in the fleet (e.g., "Linux/UNIX" or "Windows"). Configuring this argument ensures that the fleet provisions instances compatible with the desired platform, aligning with application requirements or compliance needs.

blocks.llm_summary: The `fleet_instance_set` configuration block within the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource defines the specifications and parameters for individual instance types or groups within an EC2 Fleet. It encapsulates settings such as instance type, weighted capacity, and launch template configurations, enabling users to customize and optimize the composition of their fleet for cost efficiency, performance, and workload requirements. Configuring this block allows detailed control over the allocation and scaling of diverse EC2 instances in a fleet.

blocks.name: launch_template_config
blocks.description: (Required) Nested argument containing EC2 Launch Template configurations. Defined below.

blocks.name: launch_template_specification
blocks.description: (Optional) Nested argument containing EC2 Launch Template to use. Defined below.

arguments.name: launch_template_id
arguments.description: (Optional) The ID of the launch template.
arguments.llm_summary: The `launch_template_id` argument in the `launch_template_specification` block of the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource allows users to specify the unique identifier of an existing EC2 launch template to define instance configuration details for the fleet. By setting this argument, users can streamline the provisioning of instances with pre-defined settings such as AMI, instance type, and networking, aligning with common goals like standardizing infrastructure and automating deployments.

arguments.name: launch_template_name
arguments.description: (Optional) The name of the launch template.
arguments.llm_summary: The `launch_template_name` argument in the `launch_template_specification` block of the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource allows users to specify the name of an existing EC2 launch template to define instance configuration details such as AMI, instance type, and networking settings. By setting this argument, users can streamline fleet provisioning by reusing predefined templates, ensuring consistency and simplifying the management of instance configurations across the fleet.

arguments.name: version
arguments.description: (Required) The launch template version number, `$Latest`, or `$Default.`
arguments.llm_summary: The `version` argument in the `launch_template_specification` block of the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource specifies the exact version of the launch template to use (`$Latest`, `$Default`, or a specific version number). This allows users to control which configuration of the launch template is applied when provisioning EC2 instances, ensuring consistency and alignment with desired instance settings such as AMI, instance type, and networking options.

blocks.llm_summary: The `launch_template_specification` block within the `launch_template_config` of the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource specifies the EC2 Launch Template to be used for provisioning instances in the fleet. It encapsulates settings related to the template's version and identifier, enabling users to define instance configurations such as AMI, instance type, and networking details. Configuring this block allows for precise control over instance provisioning, ensuring consistency and scalability in fleet deployments.

blocks.name: override
blocks.description: (Optional) Nested argument(s) containing parameters to override the same parameters in the Launch Template. Defined below.

arguments.name: availability_zone
arguments.description: (Optional) Availability Zone in which to launch the instances.
arguments.llm_summary: "Defines the specific Availability Zone for launching instances within the EC2 Fleet override configuration, enabling precise control over instance placement to optimize for latency, redundancy, or compliance requirements. This argument supports user goals like tailoring resource distribution across zones to meet workload or geographic constraints."

arguments.name: instance_type
arguments.description: (Optional) Instance type.
arguments.llm_summary: The `instance_type` argument in the `override` block for the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource allows users to specify the EC2 instance type for overriding default configurations within the fleet. By setting this argument, users can fine-tune the fleet's instance composition to meet specific workload requirements, such as optimizing performance, cost, or compatibility with application needs.

arguments.name: max_price
arguments.description: (Optional) Maximum price per unit hour that you are willing to pay for a Spot Instance.
arguments.llm_summary: The `max_price` argument in the `override` block of the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource allows users to define the maximum hourly price they are willing to pay for Spot Instances within the fleet. By setting this value, users can control cost optimization and ensure that instances are only provisioned if their price falls within the specified budget, aligning with common goals of cost management in cloud infrastructure.

arguments.name: priority
arguments.description: (Optional) Priority for the launch template override. If `on_demand_options` `allocation_strategy` is set to `prioritized`, EC2 Fleet uses priority to determine which launch template override to use first in fulfilling On-Demand capacity. The highest priority is launched first. The lower the number, the higher the priority. If no number is set, the launch template override has the lowest priority. Valid values are whole numbers starting at 0.
arguments.llm_summary: The `priority` argument in the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource's `override` block allows users to define the order in which launch template overrides are considered when fulfilling On-Demand capacity, specifically when the `on_demand_options` `allocation_strategy` is set to `prioritized`. By assigning a whole number (lower values indicate higher priority), users can control which override is used first, enabling fine-grained control over instance selection to optimize cost, performance, or resource allocation strategies.

arguments.name: subnet_id
arguments.description: (Optional) ID of the subnet in which to launch the instances.
arguments.llm_summary: The `subnet_id` argument in the `override` block for the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource allows users to specify the ID of the subnet where instances in the fleet will be launched, overriding default placement settings. By defining this argument, users can control the network configuration and ensure instances are deployed within a specific subnet to meet requirements such as security, connectivity, or resource isolation.

arguments.name: weighted_capacity
arguments.description: (Optional) Number of units provided by the specified instance type.
arguments.llm_summary: The `weighted_capacity` argument in the `override` block for the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource allows users to define the relative weight or capacity units assigned to a specific instance type within the fleet. By setting this value, users can influence how the fleet allocates resources and scales based on the weighted contribution of different instance types, enabling fine-grained control over cost optimization and workload distribution.

blocks.name: instance_requirements
blocks.description: (Optional) Override the instance type in the Launch Template with instance types that satisfy the requirements.

arguments.name: accelerator_manufacturers
arguments.description: (Optional) List of accelerator manufacturer names. Default is any manufacturer.
arguments.llm_summary: The `accelerator_manufacturers` argument in the `instance_requirements` block of the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource allows users to specify a set of preferred accelerator manufacturers (e.g., NVIDIA, AMD) for EC2 instances. By defining this argument, users can control the hardware compatibility of instances to meet specific workload requirements, such as machine learning or GPU-intensive tasks, ensuring alignment with their application's performance needs.

arguments.name: accelerator_names
arguments.description: (Optional) List of accelerator names. Default is any acclerator.
arguments.llm_summary: The `accelerator_names` argument in the `instance_requirements` block of the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource allows users to specify a set of desired hardware accelerators (e.g., GPUs or FPGAs) for EC2 instances in the fleet. By defining this argument, users can ensure that the instances provisioned meet specific computational needs, such as machine learning, high-performance computing, or graphics processing, aligning the fleet's capabilities with specialized workloads.

arguments.name: accelerator_types
arguments.description: (Optional) The accelerator types that must be on the instance type. Default is any accelerator type.
arguments.llm_summary: The `accelerator_types` argument in the `instance_requirements` block of the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource allows users to specify the types of hardware accelerators (e.g., GPUs, FPGAs, or inference accelerators) required for the EC2 instances in the fleet. By defining this parameter, users can ensure that the selected instances meet specific computational needs for workloads like machine learning, high-performance computing, or data processing, aligning the fleet's capabilities with specialized application requirements.

arguments.name: allowed_instance_types
arguments.description: (Optional) The instance types to apply your specified attributes against. All other instance types are ignored, even if they match your specified attributes. You can use strings with one or more wild cards,represented by an asterisk (*). The following are examples: `c5*`, `m5a.*`, `r*`, `*3*`. For example, if you specify `c5*`, you are excluding the entire C5 instance family, which includes all C5a and C5n instance types. If you specify `m5a.*`, you are excluding all the M5a instance types, but not the M5n instance types. Maximum of 400 entries in the list; each entry is limited to 30 characters. Default is no excluded instance types. Default is any instance type. If you specify `AllowedInstanceTypes`, you can't specify `ExcludedInstanceTypes`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `allowed_instance_types` argument in the `instance_requirements` block of the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource allows users to explicitly define a set of EC2 instance types (or patterns using wildcards) that meet their fleet's requirements, ensuring only specified instance types are considered for provisioning. This enables precise control over instance selection, aligning with workload needs or cost optimization strategies, while excluding all other instance types from consideration.

arguments.name: bare_metal
arguments.description: (Optional) Indicate whether bare metal instace types should be `included`, `excluded`, or `required`. Default is `excluded`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `bare_metal` argument in the `instance_requirements` block of the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource allows users to specify whether bare metal instance types should be included, excluded, or required when provisioning EC2 instances. This configuration impacts the fleet's hardware selection, enabling users to tailor their infrastructure for workloads that require direct access to physical hardware, such as high-performance computing or specialized applications.

arguments.name: burstable_performance
arguments.description: (Optional) Indicates whether burstable performance T instance types are `included`, `excluded`, or `required`. Default is `excluded`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `burstable_performance` argument in the `instance_requirements` block of the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource allows users to specify whether burstable performance T instance types should be included, excluded, or required in the fleet's instance selection criteria. This configuration impacts the fleet's ability to utilize cost-efficient, burstable instances for workloads with variable CPU performance needs, aligning instance selection with performance and budget goals.

arguments.name: cpu_manufacturers
arguments.description: (Optional) The CPU manufacturers to include. Default is any manufacturer. ~> NOTE: Don't confuse the CPU hardware manufacturer with the CPU hardware architecture. Instances will be launched with a compatible CPU architecture based on the Amazon Machine Image (AMI) that you specify in your launch template.
arguments.llm_summary: The `cpu_manufacturers` argument within the `instance_requirements` block of the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource allows users to specify a set of preferred CPU hardware manufacturers (e.g., Intel, AMD) for EC2 instances in the fleet. By defining this argument, users can optimize instance selection based on compatibility, performance preferences, or licensing requirements, ensuring the fleet aligns with workload-specific needs while maintaining flexibility for AMI-based CPU architecture compatibility.

arguments.name: excluded_instance_types
arguments.description: (Optional) The instance types to exclude. You can use strings with one or more wild cards, represented by an asterisk (*). The following are examples: `c5*`, `m5a.*`, `r*`, `*3*`. For example, if you specify `c5*`, you are excluding the entire C5 instance family, which includes all C5a and C5n instance types. If you specify `m5a.*`, you are excluding all the M5a instance types, but not the M5n instance types. Maximum of 400 entries in the list; each entry is limited to 30 characters. Default is no excluded instance types. If you specify `AllowedInstanceTypes`, you can't specify `ExcludedInstanceTypes`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `excluded_instance_types` argument in the `instance_requirements` block of the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource allows users to define a set of EC2 instance types to exclude from consideration when launching instances in the fleet. By specifying patterns with wildcards (e.g., `c5*`, `m5a.*`), users can prevent certain instance families or specific types from being used, ensuring alignment with workload requirements, cost constraints, or compliance policies. This argument is particularly useful for refining fleet composition and avoiding undesired instance types when optimizing for performance or pricing.

arguments.name: instance_generations
arguments.description: (Optional) Indicates whether current or previous generation instance types are included. The current generation instance types are recommended for use. Valid values are `current` and `previous`. Default is `current` and `previous` generation instance types.
arguments.llm_summary: The `instance_generations` argument in the `instance_requirements` block of the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource allows users to specify whether the fleet should include current-generation or previous-generation EC2 instance types. By defining this parameter, users can control the compatibility and performance characteristics of the instances in their fleet, aligning with goals such as optimizing for modern hardware or maintaining support for legacy workloads.

arguments.name: local_storage
arguments.description: (Optional) Indicate whether instance types with local storage volumes are `included`, `excluded`, or `required`. Default is `included`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `local_storage` argument in the `instance_requirements` block of the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource allows users to specify whether EC2 instance types with local storage volumes should be included, excluded, or required in the fleet's provisioning criteria. By configuring this argument, users can control the presence of ephemeral storage in their instances to align with workload needs, such as optimizing for high-performance temporary storage or excluding instances without local storage for data-sensitive applications.

arguments.name: local_storage_types
arguments.description: (Optional) List of local storage type names. Valid values are `hdd` and `ssd`. Default any storage type.
arguments.llm_summary: The `local_storage_types` argument in the `instance_requirements` block of the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource allows users to specify the preferred types of local storage (`hdd` or `ssd`) for EC2 instances in the fleet. By setting this argument, users can optimize instance selection based on storage performance needs, ensuring alignment with workload requirements such as high-speed data access or cost-effective storage.

arguments.name: max_spot_price_as_percentage_of_optimal_on_demand_price
arguments.description: (Optional) The price protection threshold for Spot Instances. This is the maximum you’ll pay for a Spot Instance, expressed as a percentage higher than the cheapest M, C, or R instance type with your specified attributes. When Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling selects instance types with your attributes, we will exclude instance types whose price is higher than your threshold. The parameter accepts an integer, which Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling interprets as a percentage. To turn off price protection, specify a high value, such as 999999. Conflicts with `spot_max_price_percentage_over_lowest_price`
arguments.llm_summary: The `max_spot_price_as_percentage_of_optimal_on_demand_price` argument allows users to define a price protection threshold for Spot Instances within the `instance_requirements` of an `aws_ec2_fleet`. By specifying a percentage above the cheapest M, C, or R instance types that meet the desired attributes, users can control cost optimization and exclude overly expensive instance types, ensuring budget-conscious fleet provisioning.

arguments.name: on_demand_max_price_percentage_over_lowest_price
arguments.description: (Optional) The price protection threshold for On-Demand Instances. This is the maximum you’ll pay for an On-Demand Instance, expressed as a percentage higher than the cheapest M, C, or R instance type with your specified attributes. When Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling selects instance types with your attributes, we will exclude instance types whose price is higher than your threshold. The parameter accepts an integer, which Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling interprets as a percentage. To turn off price protection, specify a high value, such as 999999. Default is 20. If you set `target_capacity_unit_type` to `vcpu` or `memory-mib`, the price protection threshold is applied based on the per-vCPU or per-memory price instead of the per-instance price.
arguments.llm_summary: The `on_demand_max_price_percentage_over_lowest_price` argument in the `instance_requirements` block of the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource allows users to define a price protection threshold for On-Demand Instances, expressed as a percentage above the lowest-priced compatible instance type. By configuring this, users can control cost optimization by excluding instance types that exceed the specified price limit, ensuring budget-conscious instance selection while maintaining flexibility in resource provisioning.

arguments.name: require_hibernate_support
arguments.description: (Optional) Indicate whether instance types must support On-Demand Instance Hibernation, either `true` or `false`. Default is `false`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `require_hibernate_support` argument in the `instance_requirements` block of the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource allows users to specify whether selected instance types must support On-Demand Instance Hibernation. Setting this to `true` ensures that only instance types capable of hibernation are considered, which is useful for workloads requiring state preservation during shutdowns, while leaving it as `false` broadens the pool of eligible instance types for greater flexibility.

arguments.name: spot_max_price_percentage_over_lowest_price
arguments.description: (Optional) The price protection threshold for Spot Instances. This is the maximum you’ll pay for a Spot Instance, expressed as a percentage higher than the cheapest M, C, or R instance type with your specified attributes. When Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling selects instance types with your attributes, we will exclude instance types whose price is higher than your threshold. The parameter accepts an integer, which Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling interprets as a percentage. To turn off price protection, specify a high value, such as 999999. Default is 100. Conflicts with `max_spot_price_as_percentage_of_optimal_on_demand_price` If you set DesiredCapacityType to vcpu or memory-mib, the price protection threshold is applied based on the per vCPU or per memory price instead of the per instance price.
arguments.llm_summary: The `spot_max_price_percentage_over_lowest_price` argument allows users to define a price protection threshold for Spot Instances within the `instance_requirements` of an `aws_ec2_fleet`. By specifying a percentage above the lowest-priced compatible instance type, users can control cost optimization and exclude higher-priced instance types from selection. This helps balance budget constraints with resource requirements, particularly for workloads sensitive to Spot Instance pricing.

blocks.name: accelerator_count
blocks.description: (Optional) Block describing the minimum and maximum number of accelerators (GPUs, FPGAs, or AWS Inferentia chips). Default is no minimum or maximum limits. `min` - (Optional) Minimum. `max` - (Optional) Maximum. Set to `0` to exclude instance types with accelerators.

arguments.name: max
arguments.description: (Optional) The maximum number of vCPUs. To specify no maximum limit, omit this parameter.
arguments.llm_summary: The `max` argument within the `accelerator_count` configuration for the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource allows users to define the upper limit on the number of virtual CPUs (vCPUs) allocated to accelerators in the fleet. By setting this parameter, users can control resource scaling and cost management, ensuring the fleet does not exceed a specified compute capacity; omitting it removes any maximum constraint.

arguments.name: min
arguments.description: (Required) The minimum number of vCPUs. To specify no minimum limit, specify `0`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `min` argument for `accelerator_count` in the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource allows users to define the minimum number of vCPUs required for instances with accelerators, ensuring a baseline compute capacity for workloads that depend on hardware accelerators. Setting this value to `0` removes the minimum constraint, offering flexibility for fleets with varying instance types and accelerator configurations.

blocks.llm_summary: The `accelerator_count` block within the `instance_requirements` configuration of the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource defines constraints on the minimum and maximum number of hardware accelerators (e.g., GPUs, FPGAs, AWS Inferentia chips) for selected instance types. This block enables precise control over instance selection by excluding or prioritizing instances based on accelerator availability, helping users optimize workloads for compute-intensive tasks or exclude accelerators when unnecessary.

blocks.name: accelerator_total_memory_mib
blocks.description: (Optional) Block describing the minimum and maximum total memory of the accelerators. Default is no minimum or maximum. `min` - (Optional) The minimum amount of accelerator memory, in MiB. To specify no minimum limit, omit this parameter. `max` - (Optional) The maximum amount of accelerator memory, in MiB. To specify no maximum limit, omit this parameter.

arguments.name: max
arguments.description: (Optional) The maximum number of vCPUs. To specify no maximum limit, omit this parameter.
arguments.llm_summary: The `max` argument for `accelerator_total_memory_mib` in the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource allows users to define the upper limit for the total memory (in MiB) available to GPU or hardware accelerators in the fleet. By setting this parameter, users can control resource constraints to optimize fleet performance or cost, while omitting it removes any maximum limit, enabling unrestricted memory allocation for accelerators.

arguments.name: min
arguments.description: (Required) The minimum number of vCPUs. To specify no minimum limit, specify `0`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `min` argument for `accelerator_total_memory_mib` in the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource allows users to define the minimum amount of memory (in MiB) required for GPU or hardware accelerators in the fleet's instances. Setting this value ensures that instances meet specific performance requirements for workloads reliant on accelerator memory, while specifying `0` removes any minimum constraint, enabling broader instance selection.

blocks.llm_summary: The `accelerator_total_memory_mib` block within the `instance_requirements` context of the `aws_ec2_fleet` resource defines constraints for the minimum and maximum total memory (in MiB) required by instance accelerators, such as GPUs or specialized hardware. This configuration enables users to fine-tune fleet provisioning by ensuring instances meet specific accelerator memory requirements, optimizing performance for workloads like machine learning, high-performance computing, or graphics processing.

blocks.name: baseline_ebs_bandwidth_mbps
